title: Chatflow drip batcher & KV fragment coordinator for low-jitter streaming
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: Streaming chat completions suffer from uneven latency/jitter and memory pressure when sessions send bursts of short messages or when KV fragments (prefixes) accumulate across many concurrent sessions. Goal: Implement a new batch formation heuristic ("drip" batcher) plus a KV fragment coordinator that reduces tail-latency for chat streaming while keeping GPU memory within target utilization (<= 78%). Deliverables: 1) drip batcher proto (token-level micro-batches with interleaving), 2) KV fragment coordinator (fragment coalescing + slot reservation), 3) GPU slab reservation policy and low-memory graceful fallback, 4) metrics dashboard and regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: Tail P95 latency for 99th percentile concurrent chat sessions reduced by >= 20% on benchmark workload
GPU memory high-water mark reduced by >= 12% on mixed-size chat workload compared to baseline
No increase in average token cost beyond 3% for standard prompt distributions
End-to-end tests covering streaming, re-delay, and failover scenarios added to CI
Feature toggle present for rollout with canary traffic and automatic fallback to legacy batcher
decisions: Use micro-drip batches sized by token arrival time window (configurable 8-30ms) rather than strict per-session byte thresholds
Prefer interleaved token packing across sessions to maximize GPU utilization while preserving per-session ordering
Implement light-weight KV fragment coalescer that merges adjacent small fragments with same model tokenization backbone to reduce number of KV slots
Adopt slab reservation for 'hot' sessions: reserve small GPU slab (configurable percentage) to avoid eviction storms under bursty load
Fallback policy: if slab cannot be satisfied, degrade to 'deferred-emit' where tokens are buffered server-side with an HTTP 102 interim message to client
tradeoffs: Micro-drip batching lowers jitter but can slightly increase per-token overhead due to more frequent kernel launches; mitigated by interleaving and batching multiple micro-drips together on the GPU
Aggressive KV fragment coalescing reduces slot count but may increase KV lookup times for long-running sessions — we limit coalescing window and maintain metadata for quick index lookup
Slab reservation reduces eviction jitter for hot sessions but can reduce peak throughput for best-effort customers; slab percentage will be configurable per deployment tier
Deferred-emit fallback maintains correctness but introduces extra client-visible buffering that must be documented and surfaced via Console SLO metrics
